channel.title: LLM ThreatIntel
channel.description: Threat intelligence tracking malicious LLM tools, GenAI-assisted malware, supply chain compromises, LLMjacking operations, shadow AI risks, and nation-state GenAI adoption.

item.title: Arctic Wolf Reports AntiFox Agentic Pentest Platform Used for AWS Credential Theft
item.description: Attackers are hosting self managed AntiFox instances on Alibaba Cloud and using the open source agentic penetration testing platform to target internet facing web services and AWS environments. Arctic Wolf observed AntiFox linked infrastructure making authenticated AWS API calls using valid IAM users and assumed EC2 roles, tied to vulnerability exploitation, webshell deployment, and AWS secret harvesting. One intrusion cycled through multiple identities and issued hundreds of API requests in roughly 30 minutes.

item.title: Depi Security Shows Prompt Injection Chain From GitHub Issue to Control of the @openai/codex npm Publish Pipeline
item.description: Depi Security disclosed an exploit chain that began with prompt injection through the OpenAI Codex GitHub Issue Labeler workflow and ended with the ability to publish to the official @openai/codex npm package. The chain combined code execution inside the agent sandbox, a sandbox escape, memory poisoning, a fake release, and abuse of an OpenID Connect token trusted by npm to reach release signing. OpenAI deployed a fix and awarded an initial $1,000 bounty; no customer side patch is required.

item.title: Railway Incident Report Attributes October 21 Breach to Attacker Hunting AI Provider Credentials for Distillation
item.description: Railway published its full incident report on 2026-11-10 for an attack that began 2026-10-20 and ran until the actor was evicted on 2026-10-21, concluding the attacker was specifically targeting AI provider credentials for sale to distributed transfer stations used in distillation. Railway stated at most 1.85 percent of workspaces, roughly 100,000, could have had environment variables decrypted, linked account tokens for 1,852 users were reset, and unauthorized spend on stolen keys was estimated at about 740,000 USD. Organizations hosting AI provider keys in PaaS build environments should rotate those credentials, audit for lateral movement, and move secrets out of build variable stores.

item.title: Microsoft Research Discloses Lazarus Weight Reprogramming Backdoor That Hijacks Dormant Neurons Without Retraining
item.description: Microsoft Research disclosed Lazarus, a backdoor technique that reprograms fewer than 10 dormant neurons in an LLM to make an agent execute attacker commands when a hidden trigger fires, with no retraining required. The poisoned model passes standard safety evaluations and behaves normally until the trigger, which can be as mundane as a date change, causing the agent to download and run attacker code with whatever access it was granted. Defenders handling open weight models should diff weights against the original publisher copy and treat model provenance and weight integrity as security controls.

item.title: strutil-core Ruby Gem Harvests 51 Credential Stores and Plants Backdoors in AI Coding Tools
item.description: A fake Ruby package named strutil-core was published to RubyGems on November 1, 2026 and its second version shipped a 5.48 MB credential stealing worm that read from 51 credential stores and wrote backdoors into AI coding tool settings. The worm adds a fake MCP server named workspace-tools that runs the malware through Node and installs SessionStart hooks that execute whenever a coding session opens. A wiper named net-health-checker deletes the victim home folder when a stolen GitHub token is revoked, so defenders must preserve evidence before rotating credentials.

item.title: Fireworks AI Expands October 2026 Breach Scope to Billing Data, Model Weights, and Datasets in LLMJacking Case
item.description: Fireworks AI published a November 9 update widening its October 2026 security incident to include account and billing information, and for a limited set of accounts, secrets, datasets, and incomplete model weights. Fireworks attributes the activity to a financially motivated cybercriminal group selling unauthorized LLM access through illicit routing gateways, a pattern Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant describe as LLMJacking. Customers with affected accounts should treat stored secrets, datasets, and partial model artifacts as exposed and rotate credentials now.

item.title: Operation Snowball DeepSeek Flash Agent Attacked a European Telecom and 13 Hosted Organizations
item.description: An exposed open directory revealed an autonomous AI intrusion harness that spent more than two weeks attacking a European telecom provider and 13 organizations hosted in its data centers and cloud. The harness runs on DeepSeek Flash and used a 78,000 character jailbreak system prompt to remove model safeguards, adapting to defenses when tools were blocked or deleted. Researchers withheld the operator IP, and the outcomes come from transcript reading rather than independent verification.

item.title: Cisco Talos Documents VOLTA-AUTODOXER Infostealer Using Claude to Rank Stolen Accounts
item.description: Cisco Talos disclosed a self deleting Windows infostealer, VOLTA-AUTODOXER, that steals passwords and sessions then sends the data through OpenRouter to a commercial AI model to rank the victim's assets by resale value. The malware defaults to Anthropic's Claude and fails over to other models when a refusal is detected. It harvests browser credentials, cloud keys, and AI assistant sessions, so organizations should assume any AI provider API key on a victim host is exposed.

item.title: VulnCheck Canaries Link the Microsoft Agentic AI Secret Hunter to Langflow CVE-2025-3248 Exploitation
item.description: VulnCheck canary sensors recorded the same IP central to Microsoft's agentic AI secret hunting report, 199.19.77.84, exploiting Langflow via CVE-2025-3248 to read credentials directly from hosts. The operator ran 11 payload stages over about 36 minutes in a pattern resembling an autonomous agent working a target. The activity persisted one day after Microsoft published, so defenders should treat this infrastructure as still active.

item.title: RH-ISAC Analysis Details NIK C2 ai_generate Command and OPENAI_API_KEY Harvesting on Victim Hosts
item.description: RH-ISAC published a threat intel analysis on 2026-11-02 detailing NIK C2, a Go based Windows command and control framework that integrates the OpenAI Chat Completions API through an ai_generate command so operators can issue prompts from an infected host. The analysis states the implant can use an attacker supplied API key or attempt to read the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable from the victim, which shifts API consumption and billing onto a compromised account. Defenders should monitor for unexpected outbound calls to the OpenAI API from Windows endpoints, alert on processes reading OPENAI_API_KEY, and rotate any exposed AI API keys found in host environments.

item.title: Greeter Exploit Framework Turns Exposed Flowise AI Servers Into Cloud Credential Theft Entry Points
item.description: Era Security discovered Greeter, a Chinese language exploit framework that abuses CVE-2024-58351 in end of life Flowise deployments to inject payloads per request through the overrideConfig.javascriptFunction parameter, leaving stored chatflows unmodified and logs showing only repeated 'hello' messages. Shodan data cited by TechTarget shows 4,372 Flowise instances still internet facing, 3,277 with a recognizable version, and 703 with no authentication, and Greeter uses the compromised host to probe cloud metadata services for temporary AWS IAM or Google Cloud tokens. Defenders should inventory internet facing Flowise, upgrade past 2.1.4 or retire it, require authentication, and alert on overrideConfig javascriptFunction usage and instance metadata queries.

item.title: Check Point Research Bypasses ChatGPT Lockdown Mode for Silent Chat Exfiltration and Phishing
item.description: Check Point Research discovered a vulnerability that bypassed OpenAI Lockdown Mode, allowing silent exfiltration of entire chat history, credential phishing, and malware delivery. In the Electron based ChatGPT Classic application the attack required zero user interaction, so simply holding a conversation was enough to trigger silent data exfiltration. OpenAI deployed a fix on September 18, 2026, by removing the allow-popups and allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox permissions from the outer HTML preview sandbox iframe.

item.title: Microsoft Reports Agentic AI Framework Scanning GitHub for Exposed Secrets and Abusing Azure Key Vault
item.description: Microsoft Threat Intelligence observed threat actors using an agentic AI offensive framework, ARTEX, to scan public GitHub repositories for exposed secrets and advance from discovery to Azure Key Vault data exfiltration in about five minutes. The same campaign used valid leaked or stolen application credentials for service principal sign ins across dozens of Microsoft Entra ID tenants beginning October 28, 2026, and abused compromised Azure AI services. Defenders should rotate exposed application credentials, audit service principal sign ins from the listed IP addresses, and monitor Azure Key Vault and Storage Account access.

item.title: OpenAI Cyber Model Pipeline Validates 948 Linux Local Privilege Escalation Exploits at $1,279 Each
item.description: OpenAI reported that an autonomous vulnerability discovery, exploitation, and patching pipeline using an upcoming cyber model identified and analyzed 2,308 candidate Linux kernel findings, dynamically reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities, and produced 948 working local privilege escalation exploits in a mid-October 2026 run at a total API cost of $1,213,430, or $1,279 per exploit. The pipeline also generated 291 information leak proofs of concept and produced candidate patches that OpenAI is submitting to maintainers through Patch the Planet partners. This demonstrates that AI driven exploit generation is economically viable at scale, so defenders should prioritize patch velocity for local privilege escalation bugs.

item.title: Attackers Steal AI Access Tokens from Developer Platforms Chainstack and WorkOS Using Artex Framework
item.description: SecurityWeek reported a wave of intrusions against at least a dozen AI developer platforms, with the most recent disclosures from Chainstack, WorkOS, Northflank, Trigger.dev, CommandCode and Chainstack, in which attackers hunted AI access tokens to monetize and used the open source Artex penetration testing framework for automation. Chainstack said an October 26 intrusion reached a customer database with names, member email addresses and password hashes, while WorkOS said a compromised internal sales application exposed contact details and customer communication summaries on October 30. Defenders running AI gateways, inference accounts or developer consoles should rotate provider keys and platform secrets and assume that one compromised intermediary can expose keys for many downstream inference accounts.

item.title: Check Point Research Names Haiou Jailbreak Bundle as Prompt Adware Injecting Ads for an LLM Gateway
item.description: Check Point Research analyzed the Haiou jailbreak bundle, a public prompt package targeting OpenAI Codex, and classified it as prompt adware because it persistently rewrites an agent trusted instructions and configuration files to inject advertisements for the author LLM gateway. The bundle also installs security focused Skills for penetration testing, cracking, reverse engineering and game security, and was observed in use by a cybercrime actor alongside Cobalt Strike, VulnClaw and the Ladon framework. Defenders should treat agent configuration artifacts and installed Skills as security relevant code, not benign text.

item.title: SecurityWeek Reports Cursor Marketplace Served Malicious Claude Code Extension Versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313
item.description: SecurityWeek reported that malicious versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 of the anthropic.claude-code extension were published to the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace on 29 October 2026 and stayed available for about 11 hours, potentially reaching roughly 5,000 developer systems. The extension ran JavaScript at module load to gather host reconnaissance and then attempted an SSH key install, reverse tunnel and persistence, though Cursor says the SSH step failed on most systems because it requires admin rights. Cursor users should remove the affected versions, run the Cursor detection script, and rotate credentials from any host that loaded the extension.

item.title: Warp Discloses Vendor Infrastructure Exploitation Exposing Agent Decision Logs and Telemetry
item.description: Warp founder Zach Lloyd disclosed on 27 October 2026 active and narrow exploitation of a vendor in Warp infrastructure, exposing agent decision logs and telemetry for an estimated 1 percent of users. Warp says it detected the activity within hours, notified identified users, engaged external help and informed law enforcement, and did not clarify whether source code, prompts, or credentials were included in the exposed logs. Affected users should rotate credentials and review agent activity, because the scope of the exposed data remains undefined.

item.title: JFrog Analyzes testmetest npm Worm Hijacking 42 GitHub Repositories with AI Agent Execution Hooks
item.description: JFrog Security Research analyzed an npm worm, tracked as testmetest, that hijacked 42 GitHub repositories across 11 legitimate owners and planted a 12.9 to 13.7 MB payload at .github/init.js alongside agent configuration files for Claude Code, Gemini, Cursor, and VS Code. The payload harvested GitHub and npm credentials, propagated through available npm publishing permissions including GitHub OIDC token exchange, and installs a wiper that deletes the victim home directory when the stolen GitHub token is revoked, turning routine cleanup into data loss. Defenders should isolate affected hosts before revoking tokens and audit repositories for unauthorized .github/init.js and agent config changes.

item.title: GitLab Warns of Critical Remote Code Execution in AI Gateway CVE-2026-90970
item.description: GitLab warned customers to immediately patch a critical AI Gateway vulnerability that could let attackers run arbitrary commands on vulnerable instances. BleepingComputer reported the flaw as CVE-2026-90970 and said it stems from improper handling that enables remote code execution. Teams running GitLab AI Gateway should apply the vendor patch without delay and check exposed instances for signs of command execution.
